AI Planning Platform Pigment Raises $250M Series E at $2.3B Valuation
・
버섯돌이(Taehyun Kim)
      
Pigment, the AI business planning and performance management platform, has raised a $250 million Series E at a $2.3 billion valuation. The round was led by the Scaleup Europe Fund, managed by EQT, with new investor WIL (World Innovation Lab) joining existing backers Greenoaks, ICONIQ, IVP, and Meritech. Nvidia has also said it plans to invest — CEO Jensen Huang announced the stake in Paris on October 13 — though the amount hasn’t been disclosed.
Beyond the Chatbot: Selling the Calculation Model Itself
Pigment connects a company’s finance, sales, and workforce data on a single platform, then lets AI agents build and run plans directly on top of it — what the company calls “autonomous planning.” It’s a concrete example of generative AI moving past answering questions in a chat window and into actually building and running the calculation models — budgets, revenue forecasts — that a business runs on. At the core is Graphite, Pigment’s proprietary compute engine, which the company says lets thousands of AI agents and people work on the same governed model simultaneously, scaling to hundreds of billions of data points with fully traceable results.
Co-founder Eléonore Crespo was previously a financial analyst at Google advising its EMEA president and CFO on strategy and planning, before becoming an investor at Index Ventures. Co-founder Romain Niccoli co-founded ad-tech company Criteo and served as its CTO. The two founded Pigment in Paris in 2019.
Past $100M ARR, Doubling Again
Pigment’s annual recurring revenue passed $100 million this year, doubling year-over-year for the second year running. Crespo told Bloomberg she expects it to double again next year, putting it near $200 million. The $2.3 billion valuation works out to roughly 23x current ARR. The company says 85% of new metrics on the platform are now created by an AI agent — a company-reported figure, not independently audited.
Its customer list includes large enterprises like Danone, DirecTV, Siemens, Snowflake, ServiceNow, and Unilever. L’Oréal is replacing its salary-planning tool for more than 95,000 employees worldwide with Pigment — a concrete example of enterprise-wide adoption at scale. Pigment also notes that AI-native, engineering-dense companies like Anthropic, ElevenLabs, and Uber chose Pigment over building the equivalent in-house.
The Turf: SAP, Oracle, and Microsoft’s Excel
Pigment is going after customers running on SAP, Oracle, IBM, Anaplan, and Microsoft. Anaplan, a major incumbent in the category, was taken private by Thoma Bravo in a $10.7 billion deal in 2022 — a reference point for how much this market is worth. Straits Research puts the enterprise performance management (EPM) market at $7.51 billion in 2026, growing at roughly 10.4% a year through 2034.
The Scaleup Europe Fund that led this round targets €5 billion, backed by the European Commission alongside private investors including Novo Holdings and Allianz; EQT was selected to manage it in May. The fund also joined Mistral’s €3 billion Series D, led by Samsung Electronics, as part of its mandate to build European tech companies into global leaders.
Startups Chasing the Same Spot
Pigment isn’t the only one going after this space. Abacum, which started in Barcelona and now focuses mainly on the U.S. market, raised a $60 million Series B in June 2025 led by Scale Venture Partners (with Cathay Innovation, Y Combinator, Creandum, and others participating; total funding is around $90 million). Abacum targets a smaller mid-market customer base than Pigment — a different position in the same category.
Israel’s Datarails raised a $70 million Series C on January 21 this year, led by One Peak, bringing total funding to $175 million at an estimated $550 million valuation. The company says 2025 revenue grew 70% year-over-year and headcount passed 400. Rather than replacing a company’s entire planning stack the way Pigment does, Datarails leans toward layering AI agents on top of the Excel models companies already use — and at an estimated revenue multiple of roughly 5.5x (versus Pigment’s roughly 23x), the market is pricing the two approaches very differently.
The category is splitting into three strategies: layer AI onto Excel (Datarails), target the mid-market (Abacum), or replace the enterprise planning stack outright (Pigment). The gap in valuation multiples shows which strategy investors are currently willing to pay the biggest premium for.
The Real Test Is Decision-Making
The harder question is what AI actually does inside finance departments. In a March Gartner survey of 204 finance leaders, 45% of finance AI investment was aimed at productivity, while only 20% targeted better decision-making. That smaller, harder category is exactly where Pigment is positioning itself — AI that doesn’t just surface numbers, but takes responsibility for building the plan and acting on it. Gartner’s 2025 survey found finance-function AI adoption at 59%, barely up from 58% the year before. There’s still a wide gap between “using AI” and “letting AI make the decision.”
That gap is worth watching for enterprise SaaS outside the U.S. and Europe, too. What actually matters in Pigment’s numbers isn’t “AI usage” — it’s passing $100 million in ARR, doubling year-over-year, and landing enterprise-wide deployments like L’Oréal’s 95,000-employee rollout. The claim that AI agents create 85% of new metrics is a striking number, but what ultimately supports the valuation is revenue growth and the scale of trust large enterprises place in the product for mission-critical work. As more enterprise SaaS companies market “built-in AI,” the metrics that actually get tested are the same ones Pigment is being judged on.

Building on Abacum Intelligence, Abacum Launches Modeler and Brings Agentic Modeling to Every Finance Team

The AI-native FP&A platform brings expert-grade modeling to every finance team. Describe the plan in natural language, and Modeler builds it on live company data in minutes, calculated by Abacum's Engine and approved by finance.
NEW YORK and BARCELONA, Spain, Oct. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Abacum, the AI-native FP&A platform, today launched Modeler, an AI agent that brings Agentic Modeling to finance teams. Starting from natural language prompts or existing spreadsheets, Modeler transforms initial inputs into live, fully functional business models instantly ready for execution.
Agentic Modeling is a new approach in which finance defines what a model needs to do, and an AI agent builds it. Instead of building a model line by line, teams set the requirements and the agent does the work. It selects the right structure from proven model blueprints, maps it to the company's connected data and lays out the full logic for review. Work that has traditionally taken days or weeks of manual build now takes minutes, and the time it gives back goes where finance teams want it: analysis, scenarios and strategic decisions.
That time matters. Building and maintaining models is one of the most time-intensive parts of the finance function, and in most companies the models that do exist live with one or two people. When those people are busy, the business waits. When they move on, every model they own is one resignation away from nobody understanding it. Modeler is built to change both.
How Agentic Modeling Works
 Build live models in minutes – ask for the model you need, such as "Build me a P&L from my GL data." Modeler scans the company's connected datasets and builds a working model with calculations across actuals and planning versions, ready to plan from day one.
 Bring what you've built – upload an Excel file and Modeler reads its lines, sections and totals, then rebuilds that model on the data already connected to Abacum, so teams don't start from scratch.
 Approve every plan – before anything is built, Modeler shows the full proposal, variable by variable, with the logic behind each one. Teams refine it in natural language, then approve or reject it. Nothing is saved without approval.
 Trust the math – Modeler proposes the structure and logic; Abacum's deterministic calculation Engine performs every calculation, exactly as it does for models built by hand.
 Explain any model – ask any model to explain its own logic, line by line: what each variable is, how they connect and how every number is calculated. New team members get up to speed without reverse-engineering someone else's work.
 Grow any model – add variables, and add, edit or remove sections in existing models, just by asking.
Time back for the work that matters
With Modeler, the hours that used to go into building go into using the model. A headcount plan the VP of Finance needs by Friday is ready the same morning. A new revenue model for the board starts as a request, not a blank canvas. A question about how a forecast is calculated gets answered on the spot, without waiting for the one person who built it. Finance teams move faster, and the expertise stays with the team.
Commenting on the launch of Modeler, Julio Martínez, Co-Founder and CEO of Abacum, said: "Finance has been told to do more with less for as long as anyone can remember. We think that promise has run its course. Modeler is about doing more with more: more models, built in minutes instead of weeks, by more of the team, with less lift than it has ever taken. The agent does the building, Abacum's Engine still does the math, and finance still approves every model. What changes is how fast you get there, and who gets to build."
Martínez continues: "Every finance leader knows the model that lives in one person's head. That isn't a modeling problem, it's a resilience problem. When more of the team can ask for a model, see exactly how it works, refine it with natural language, and ask it to explain itself, the model belongs to the business. That's what AI-native should mean: not AI bolted onto the side of a platform, but a finance team that is AI-native itself."
What's next
Modeler is the first step in Abacum's agentic modeling roadmap. Later this year, it will bring complete workbooks into Abacum, including formulas and multi-tab files, and will extend editing deeper into existing models, so teams can refine what they've built as easily as they create it.
Availability
Modeler is available today to all Abacum customers as standard functionality, included in the Abacum platform at no additional cost. To see Modeler in action, visit .
About Abacum
Abacum is the AI-native business planning platform. Built first for finance and extended to every department, Abacum holds a company's data, business logic and context in one governed layer, where AI agents and teams plan the business together. Agents own the recurring workflows; people own the judgment. More than 500 customers in over 40 countries run their planning on Abacum, including DISH, ThoughtSpot, Strava, Acorns and Replit. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in New York, with offices in Toronto, Barcelona, Buenos Aires and the UK, Abacum is backed by more than $100 million from investors including Scale Venture Partners, Atomico and Y Combinator. Quick Summary
AccountsIQ and Abacum have formed a strategic partnership to provide mid-market businesses with an integrated AI-powered finance stack. By combining cloud accounting with advanced FP&A tools, the collaboration eliminates manual spreadsheets, enabling automated real-time financial forecasting and multi-entity consolidation for over 35,000 global users.
How Does the AccountsIQ and Abacum Partnership Benefit Finance Teams?
The integration of AccountsIQ and Abacum addresses the critical need for automated data flows in mid-market organizations. By linking multi-currency cloud accounting directly to an AI-native FP&A platform, finance professionals can transition from simple record-keeping to strategic business planning without the risk of manual entry errors. Key benefits include:
   Automated reporting that replaces traditional, error-prone spreadsheets.
   Real-time decision-making powered by actuals flowing directly from accounting to planning modules.
   Multi-entity consolidation with built-in FX conversion for international operations.
This AI-powered finance stack allows teams to focus on high-value analysis rather than data gathering, significantly reducing the time spent on monthly reporting cycles.
Image 7: FTT Fintech Festival London
What Results Has This Integrated Technology Delivered?
Early adoption by firms like investment bank GP Bullhound demonstrates the practical impact of this cloud accounting integration. The bank utilized a custom connector to manage its multi-entry structure, replacing manual uploads with automated synchronization. The partnership leverages Abacum's platform, which has secured $90 million in funding, to serve customers across more than 30 countries. AccountsIQ brings a robust infrastructure supporting 35,000+ users and 30+ technology integrations, ensuring that financial intelligence is scalable for high-growth companies.
How Does This Move the Needle for AI-Powered Finance?
The shift from backward-looking reporting to forward-looking strategic planning is the core value proposition of this alliance. By acting as an intelligence layer, Abacum transforms raw data from AccountsIQ into actionable insights. This partnership is specifically designed for modern European businesses looking to scale with confidence by utilizing clean, consolidated numbers across complex global operations.
FF NEWS TAKE:
This partnership definitely moves the needle for the mid-market. While enterprise-level firms have long enjoyed integrated AI-powered finance stack solutions, mid-market players have often been stuck between basic accounting software and manual spreadsheets. By bridging the gap between cloud accounting and sophisticated FP&A, AccountsIQ and Abacum are democratizing high-end financial intelligence, making real-time financial forecasting a standard requirement rather than a luxury for growing businesses.

Your questions, answered
Answers about planning, onboarding, governance, and more.
Which systems does Abacum integrate with for financial services?
Abacum connects to Snowflake, BigQuery, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks, Xero, Salesforce, Stripe, Chargebee, and payroll systems including ADP, Workday and Rippling. Connections run continuously rather than as nightly batches, so actuals update through the month rather than only at close. Coverage is deepest across modern finance stacks, and less common or industry-specific systems may need custom API work.
Does Abacum handle multi-entity planning and consolidation?
Abacum plans and reports across multiple legal entities in one model, translating local currencies into your reporting currency at FX rates you set. Group roll-ups, variance analysis and board reporting all work at that level. Abacum is a planning system rather than a statutory consolidation tool, so it does not calculate intercompany eliminations or produce statutory filings.
How does Abacum keep forecast assumptions auditable?
Every figure in Abacum traces back to the formula and source data behind it. Assumptions are held as named drivers rather than buried in cells, and version history records what changed between plan versions and who changed it. Permissions control who can edit each input, so a reviewer can inspect any number without rebuilding the model.
Can Abacum plan headcount and cost against revenue drivers?
Yes. Headcount is planned as a driver inside the same model as revenue, so roles, start dates, ramp and fully loaded cost flow straight into margin and cash. Each cost center or entity can own its own inputs, and changes cascade into group reporting without re-keying or a separate workforce planning tool.
What does Abacum Intelligence do, and can finance teams check its work?
Abacum Intelligence drafts formulas, detects anomalies in incoming actuals, and writes first-pass variance explanations. It works inside your existing model rather than as a separate chat tool. Every suggestion shows the formula and the source figures behind it, so an analyst can verify the reasoning before it reaches a board pack.
Does Abacum replace our ERP or accounting system?
No. Abacum sits on top of your ERP, data warehouse and payroll systems, reading actuals from them continuously and adding the planning, forecasting and reporting layer above. Your general ledger stays the system of record. Most financial services teams keep NetSuite or Sage Intacct in place and use Abacum for everything downstream of the close.
What does onboarding involve?
Onboarding is designed to help teams establish connected data, core models, and planning workflows around their operating needs. Most teams go live in about 6 weeks. Timeline depends on your data complexity, number of entities, and workflows involved. Our implementation team will scope specifics with you during onboarding.
How does Abacum support governance?
Permissions, shared workflows, and connected models help finance maintain control over sensitive data and planning processes.

Why Most FP&A Stacks Stop Scaling. And What Abacum Solves
More products. More regions. More teams are asking "what if?" The business moves faster every quarter, but planning and reporting struggle to keep up. Finance ends up rechecking numbers instead of steering the plan. Here is the pattern we keep seeing, and what Abacum was built to solve.
01
TOO MANY VERSIONS OF THE TRUTH
Actuals live in the ERP. Assumptions live in three spreadsheets. Plans live in a fourth. Every quarter, finance spends days re-checking numbers and re-mapping data across systems before any actual analysis can start. By the time the team has a defensible view of the business, the assumptions behind it have already shifted. Planning is happening, but it is happening to the wrong version of the truth.
02
MODELS THAT CANNOT KEEP UP
A pricing change, a new hire plan, or an org shift triggers hours of rework. The model you built last quarter no longer reflects how the business runs. Updating it requires a systems project, a consultant contract, or a week of one analyst's time. By the time the model catches up to the business, the business has moved again, and the model is back out of sync.
03
REPORTING THAT DRIVES DRIFT
Leadership asks a question. Finance cannot answer in minutes. The board wants to know why the forecast moved. Sales wants to know why their territory's variance changed. The CEO wants a what-if on hiring. None of these questions can be answered without going back to the data, rebuilding the calculation, and emailing the answer back two days later. Leaders move on instinct because finance cannot move at the pace of the conversation.
04
THE PROCESS THAT NEVER GETS PROJECT-MANAGED
Finance becomes the project manager for everyone's spreadsheets. Department leads send their plans late. Templates change between cycles. Consolidation requires four hours of cell-mapping every month. The FP&A team's actual job, analysis, scenario planning, and decision support get crowded out by the cell-by-cell coordination work that the planning process produces.
If two or more of these describe your current planning cycle, the stack is the bottleneck, not the team running it.

Yes. We are an Abacum implementation and licensing reseller partner, which means we can quote and resell Abacum licenses directly, bundled with implementation. What kind of company is Abacum built for?
Abacum is built for FP&A teams that have outgrown Excel-led planning but need a platform finance can run without specialist admins or long change cycles. Typical buyer: mid-market to enterprise companies with multiple business units, multi-entity consolidation needs, and an FP&A team scaling alongside the business. The platform is designed for finance ownership rather than IT or platform-admin dependency, which makes it a different operating model than legacy enterprise FP&A platforms.
How long does an Abacum implementation typically take?
Abacum's published guidance is that implementations move quickly relative to legacy FP&A platforms. In practice, deployments range from 6 to 12 weeks depending on integration complexity, the number of business units in scope, and the maturity of your existing planning process. Companies with clean data and a defined planning cycle land closer to six weeks. Companies migrating from a complex Adaptive or Anaplan environment, with multi-entity consolidation and dozens of integrations, land closer to twelve. We scope each engagement against your actual data condition and integration requirements before committing to a timeline.
